Meta.title: Chameleon — a walk through the jungle canopy
Meta.description: Walk along a jungle branch with a chameleon: how it changes colour, looks two ways at once, hunts with its tongue and holds on with its feet.

hero.label: 01 · emerald coat
hero.title: Chameleon
hero.tagline: The slowest hunter in the canopy. <accent>And the most patient.</accent>
hero.p1: Its name comes from the Greek khamaileōn, “ground lion”. There are around two hundred species, and about half of them live only on Madagascar.
hero.p2: Scroll down, and this one will walk you along its branch.

color.label: 02 · turquoise coat
color.title: Colour is a mood, <accent>not a mask</accent>
color.p1: Under a chameleon's skin lie cells packed with tiny guanine crystals. When the animal relaxes or gets excited, the spacing between the crystals changes, and so does the light they reflect: green turns turquoise, yellow or a startled red.
color.p2: Camouflage is mostly a side effect. Chameleons change colour to warm up, to cool down and above all to talk: to court a mate, to warn off a rival, or to say “I give up”.

eyes.label: 03 · macaw-yellow coat
eyes.title: Two eyes, <accent>two directions</accent>
eyes.p1: Each eye sits in a turret of skin and swivels on its own, so a chameleon can watch the leaf above and the branch behind at the same time, almost the whole sphere around it, without turning its head.
eyes.p2: When something tasty appears, both eyes swing forward and lock onto it. Only then does the chameleon judge the distance and get ready to strike.

tongue.label: 04 · fuchsia coat
tongue.title: A tongue <accent>faster than a blink</accent>
tongue.p1: The tongue is bunched around a slender bone in the throat, like a spring pressed over a rod. Released, it can shoot out to twice the length of the body; in the smallest species it goes from rest to about 100 km/h in a hundredth of a second.
tongue.p2: The tip is a muscular cup coated in mucus hundreds of times thicker than human saliva, sticky enough to haul back an insect or even a small lizard.

grip.label: 05 · tropical orange coat
grip.title: Feet like tongs, <accent>a tail like a hand</accent>
grip.p1: A chameleon's toes are fused into two bundles, two on one side and three on the other, so every foot closes around a branch like a pair of tongs.
grip.p2: The tail is a fifth hand: it curls round a twig for balance and coils up like a spring when it isn't needed. On the move, the chameleon rocks back and forth like a leaf in the wind.

night.label: 06 · night coat, with gold
night.title: At night the jungle <accent>goes quiet</accent>
night.p1: When the light goes, chameleons climb out to the thinnest twigs, where any snake would shake the branch long before it got close, and fall asleep. Many turn pale in their sleep and are easy to spot with a torch.
night.p2: Some species keep one more secret: under ultraviolet light, small bumps on their skulls glow blue — bone shining through thin skin.

Footer.text: End of the branch. Good night.
